title: Normalized continuous coefficient completion for compact principal-adic domains
statement: Let A be a compact Hausdorff topological commutative domain [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring], p a nonzero element, and assume every A/(p)^(n+1) is finite and its quotient fibres form a neighbourhood basis at each point. For any scheme T [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the actual pulled-back continuous coefficient ring has a unique isomorphism with the inverse limit of the positive constant quotient tower of ULift A [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-adic-lisse-module]. Each projection carries a scalar constant to its residue, using precisely the canonical constant-function comparison [lem-sf-finite-discrete-normalized-encoding]. No Noetherian or sheaf-module flatness assertion is part of this statement.

source.place: Steps 1--4, expressed for compact principal-adic domains; scalar uniqueness uses the open-fibre argument below.

proof.text: Write I=(p). The asserted neighbourhood basis makes every quotient map A→A/I^(n+1) locally constant: every point has the corresponding fibre as a neighbourhood. Its fibres are closed as well, because their complements are unions of the other open fibres. They separate distinct points by the Hausdorff property. Thus A is totally disconnected.

source.place: Steps 1--4, expressed for compact principal-adic domains; scalar uniqueness uses the open-fibre argument below.

proof.text: For any compatible sequence of residues, the inverse images in A are nonempty nested closed sets. Compactness gives a point in their intersection, unique because the quotient fibres form a Hausdorff neighbourhood basis. This is an isomorphism of rings between A and the inverse limit of its finite quotients. The map is continuous coordinatewise, and the inverse is continuous by the same fibre neighbourhood basis.

proof.text: The canonical continuous-ring realization identifies the pulled-back internal coefficient ring with the sheaf of continuous A-valued functions on each pro-etale object. The canonical adjoint comparison sends scalar constants to constant functions: apply its defining adjunction bijection to the constant continuous function. Reconstructing section rings preserves this equality and the ring operations.

source.place: Steps 1--4, expressed for compact principal-adic domains; scalar uniqueness uses the open-fibre argument below.

proof.text: For each finite discrete quotient, the constant-preserving comparison with its continuous-function sheaf is an isomorphism. On every object a function is locally constant on the open fibres of its values, giving local surjectivity; on a nonempty object equality of constant functions implies equality of scalars, and the empty cover handles the empty object. These comparisons commute with every quotient transition. Continuous functions into the compact ring limit are exactly compatible continuous coordinate functions. Sectionwise limits therefore construct the required ring-sheaf isomorphism, normalized on every scalar.

source.place: Steps 1--4, expressed for compact principal-adic domains; scalar uniqueness uses the open-fibre argument below.

proof.text: To prove uniqueness fix n. For a continuous A-valued function f, restrict to open fibres of its residue modulo p^(n+1), and choose a scalar a lifting each residue. There f-a belongs pointwise to p^(n+1)A. Multiplication by the nonzero p^(n+1) is injective on the domain A, hence is a homeomorphism onto its image by compactness and Hausdorffness. Its inverse gives a continuous g with f=a+p^(n+1)g. A normalized ring comparison followed by the n-th projection sends this expression to the residue of a, since it kills p^(n+1). Thus any two candidates have identical finite projections on this cover, hence globally. Joint monicity of limit projections identifies their homomorphisms and hence their ring isomorphisms.

theorem compact_adic_continuous_identification
    (A : Type u) [CommRing A] [IsDomain A] [TopologicalSpace A] [IsTopologicalRing A]
    [CompactSpace A] [T2Space A] (p : A) (hp : p ≠ 0)
    (hf : ∀ n : ℕ, Finite (A ⧸ Ideal.span ({p} : Set A) ^ (n + 1)))
    (hb : ∀ x : A, (𝓝 x).HasBasis (fun _ : ℕ ↦ True) (fun n ↦
      {y | Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({p} : Set A) ^ (n + 1)) y =
        Ideal.Quotient.mk (Ideal.span ({p} : Set A) ^ (n + 1)) x}))
    (T : Scheme.{u}) :
    (∃! e : InternalAbelianSheafModule.sectionRingSheaf.{u + 1, u + 1, u}
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
      (condensedRingObj (Profinite.continuousCoefficientRingObj A) T) ≅
    Scheme.adicLisseCompletedRing T
      (Ideal.span ({ULift.up p} : Set (ULift.{u + 1} A))),
    ∀ (U : T.ProEtᵒᵖ) (a : A) (n : ℕ),
      ((limit.π (Scheme.adicLisseRingSystem T
        (Ideal.span ({ULift.up p} : Set (ULift.{u + 1} A)))) (op n)).hom.app U)
        ((e.hom.hom.app U)
          ((FiniteDiscreteOrdinary.canonicalAbelianMap A T).hom.app U
            ((toSheafify (D := Ab.{u + 1}) (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
              ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj
                (AddCommGrpCat.of.{u + 1} (ULift.{u + 1} A)))).app U (ULift.up a)))) =
      (toSheafify (D := CommRingCat.{u + 1}) (Scheme.ProEt.topology T)
        ((Functor.const T.ProEtᵒᵖ).obj (CommRingCat.of
          (ULift.{u + 1} A ⧸
            (Ideal.span ({ULift.up p} : Set (ULift.{u + 1} A))) ^ (n + 1))))).app U
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk
            ((Ideal.span ({ULift.up p} : Set (ULift.{u + 1} A))) ^ (n + 1))
            (ULift.up a)))
